one_month_reasoning: Revised. I no longer expect Q3 2026 results inside the window. Booking announced its Q3 2025 date (Oct 28) on Sep 30, 2025 and its Q2 2026 date (Aug 4) on Jul 7, each about four weeks ahead. EDGAR shows no notice as of Oct 2, so the print is most likely about Nov 3, after the Oct 30 close that ends the window. I put P(print in window) at about 15%. Scheduled events that are inside the window: the FOMC on Oct 27-28 (after the Sep 16 hike to 3.75-4.00%), continuing AI-agent headlines (Muse has held #1 on the US App Store since Sep 18; per Sensor Tower it passed 3.4M downloads; Google AI Mode agentic hotel booking is in US testing, with Booking.com and Priceline among the launch partners), and possibly peer pre-announcements. I removed my round-1 earnings widening and the slight beat tilt. The distribution is a near-lognormal with median about $159.6 and sigma about 11.2% (38-39% annual vol / 3.5), mixed 85/15 with a wider (14%) component for the chance the print lands in the window. Near the lows there is some reversal potential, but it is offset by negative momentum and headline risk, so I applied no tilt.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (NTM EPS at Oct 2027 ~$12.95 x 15x = $194) and FCF yield (NTM FCF ~$10.75B / ~710M shares = ~$15.1 per share at a 7.75% yield = $195), weighted 60/40, giving ~$194. FY27 EPS is a stated ~4% haircut to the ~$12.37 consensus. Shares start from 751.4M outstanding (Jul 27, 2026), not 765M.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS at Oct 2027 ~$12.95 (0.25 x FY27 $11.90 + 0.75 x FY28 $13.30) x 15x forward P/E

inputs_detail.derivation: 39-analyst consensus as of Sep 24, 2026. It is +14.6% on $9.12, at the top of the company's low-to-mid-teens adj EPS growth guide.

A ~4% haircut to the ~$12.37 consensus, for the soft Q3 guide (EBITDA +4-6%) and the risk of AI-agent channel share going to Expedia (Muse) or of higher marketing costs. That gives ~+14% growth, of which ~6% is net share shrink (44M shares retired in H1 2026, $14.5B authorization left).
FY27 x ~1.12: ~6% operating growth (mid-single-digit room nights plus transformation savings) plus ~5-6% buyback shrink.

Today's multiple is ~13.4x NTM consensus. In round 1 I used 17x on FY27, which was inconsistent with a 7.5% FCF yield (FCF per share runs ~1.15-1.2x EPS, so 7.5% FCF is roughly 15.5-16x EPS). I now use 15x, which allows a modest relief re-rating only. Support for some relief: Booking.com is a launch partner in Google AI Mode agentic booking, it has a ChatGPT app, and its traffic leadership holds. Against a full re-rating: Muse adoption is real and verified.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: NTM FCF at Oct 2027 ~$10.75B / ~710M shares = ~$15.1 per share at a 7.75% FCF yield

inputs_detail.derivation: FY26 ~$9.7B, FY27 ~$10.3B, FY28 ~$10.9B (~6%/yr, in line with H1 2026's +7%), weighted 0.25/0.75 into FY27/FY28.

751.4M on Jul 27, 2026 (10-Q cover). H1 2026 retired 44M (~5.5%), and FCF of ~$10B less ~$1.3B of dividends funds ~5-6%/yr net shrink at $160-190. Fifteen months gives ~700M; I use ~710M to allow for SBC dilution and a higher price.

The TTM yield is ~8% today ($9.54B / ~$120B market cap). I allow a slight compression because FCF is growing and the balance sheet is clean (~$3B net debt at Q2). It stays above 7% because SBC (~$0.56B/yr) is excluded and the AI overhang persists.

bear.story: AI agents (Muse via Expedia, Google AI Mode, ChatGPT) take measurable share of hotel discovery, and Booking pays up to stay in those channels. Room nights slip to low single digits, FY27 EPS comes in at ~$11 against $12.37 consensus, and the market applies a ~10x 'structural decline' multiple to ~$11.5 NTM EPS.

base.story: EPS compounds ~13-14% (mid-single-digit room nights, ~6% share shrink). Agents become one more distribution channel in which Booking participates (Google AI Mode launch partner, ChatGPT app). The multiple recovers partly, to ~14.3x on ~$12.95 NTM EPS.

bull.story: Q3/Q4 prints and the FY27 guide show no traffic or take-rate damage. Booking proves agents need its supply and lands its own Muse/Meta or OpenAI booking deal. The AI discount narrows to ~17.5-18x on ~$13.4 NTM EPS.

thesis_break_reason: Unchanged at ~$118. That is ~9.5x FY27 consensus EPS ($12.37), ~11x FY26 ($10.45), a ~12% FCF yield, and ~21% below the $150.14 intraday 52-week low (May 20, 2026). A price there would most likely reflect falling estimates, not just multiple fear: room nights flat or negative, a guide-down, agent channels taking take-rate or forcing higher marketing spend, a large parity-damages or FTC outcome, or a travel recession. Ordinary 38% volatility from $159 does not get there without such news.

key_uncertainties: Whether consumer AI agents shift hotel bookings to Expedia (Muse) or to hotels directly, or simply become another channel where Booking competes. Muse is verified at #1 on the US App Store since Sep 18 with >3.4M downloads (Sensor Tower), but retention and booking conversion are unknown.
The economics of agent channels (Google AI Mode, ChatGPT): Booking stays merchant of record, but the take-rate and marketing costs per booking could rise.
Whether the ~13.4x NTM multiple re-rates at all within 12 months even if EPS compounds ~13%.
Macro: the Fed hiking cycle, oil above $100 and Middle East effects on long-haul travel.
Timing of the Q3 print relative to the 1-month window (likely ~Nov 3, not announced).
reasoning: Round 2 changes. (1) I accept the supervisor's facts: FY25 adj EPS is a reported $9.12; consensus is FY26 $10.45 / FY27 ~$12.37 (Sep 24, 39 analysts); shares outstanding were 751.4M on Jul 27 and are falling ~5-6%/yr; market cap is ~$120B; net debt is ~$3B at Q2 and seasonally flattered; the Q3 print is likely ~Nov 3, outside the 1-month window. (2) In my alt-data lane I dropped the LinkedIn-sourced 'Similarweb' ranking and the single-vendor Adthena click-share claim. I replaced them with Semrush traffic panels. Booking.com is still #1 in US hospitality traffic in August 2026 (62.9M visits, -9.4% m/m, a smaller seasonal drop than Marriott -15.8%, Hilton -18.1% or Hotels.com -11.8%) and #1 globally (556M visits in August vs 571M in July). These are panel estimates, but two pages of one vendor agree, and they show no visible traffic break before Muse; Muse launched Sep 8, so September data is not yet available. Muse's adoption is now verified with Sensor Tower/Appfigures data via TechCrunch: #1 US App Store since Sep 18, ~2.3-3.4M downloads. The threat is real and I no longer cite it from a crypto recap. A new finding cuts the other way: Booking.com and Priceline are among the 10 launch partners of Google AI Mode agentic hotel booking (US test, Aug 2026), with the platform remaining merchant of record, and Booking already has a ChatGPT app. So the agent channel is not closed to Booking; Muse's Expedia exclusivity is a channel-share loss, not disintermediation. The SiteMinder survey (AI as the starting point for only 4% of travelers) still stands. (3) Valuation: I fixed the internal inconsistency the supervisor flagged (17x P/E vs a 7.5% FCF yield) by using 15x NTM EPS ($12.95, with FY27 a stated 4% haircut to consensus) = $194, and a 7.75% yield on ~$15.1 FCF per share = $195. The blend is ~$194, up from $188 mainly because of the share-count correction. Scenarios 115/185/240 at 25/50/25% give a mean of ~$181. The ladder is a lognormal with median ~$175 and sigma ~0.37 (realized vol 38-39%), with a slightly fatter left tail for structural AI risk and a thinner far-right tail. The 12-month view moves up only modestly (P(>=159) 0.585 to 0.60) because the buyback and EPS corrections are partly offset by the verified Muse adoption. The 1-month ladder narrows because earnings likely fall outside the window. About 6 extra queries were used; X/Reddit were not fetched.
